CLASS 35 · AGES 4–5 · 20 COUNTING CARDS

Numbers, Counting & Early Math.

HOW THIS CLASS WORKS

Twenty numbers, one smiling fruit at a time.

This class walks a child from the very first "one" to a triumphant twenty: twenty printable cards, each with a big numeral on top, rows of smiling fruit to count underneath, and the fruit word printed below. Count the card, then count the real thing — one apple from the bowl, three orange segments on the plate, ten blueberries if you are feeling brave. The kitchen is the answer key, so practice arrives with every snack.

The set has a built-in shape worth knowing as a grown-up: cards 1 to 5 fit one hand, cards 6 to 10 need both, and cards 11 to 20 repeat one quiet pattern — a full ten, plus some more. Say that pattern out loud when you reach eleven and the whole teen decade opens at once. One card a sitting is plenty; the whole class is a month of two-minute counting moments.

MEET THE SET

One apple to twenty figs.

The cards run in three gentle waves. Cards one to five fit on one hand — one apple, two bananas, three oranges, four strawberries, five pears. Cards six to ten need both hands: six grapes, seven cherries, eight watermelon slices, nine peaches and ten blueberries in two neat rows of five. Then the teens begin — eleven kiwis, twelve lemons, thirteen pineapples, fourteen raspberries, fifteen mangoes, sixteen coconuts, seventeen apples, eighteen bananas, nineteen apricots — and twenty figs close the set in four proud rows of five.

Every card repeats the same quiet move: count the smiling fruit, say the number, then find that many real things in your own kitchen. Nothing on the cards needs a pencil, a score or a timer — just a finger and a voice. One card a sitting is plenty, and reaching twenty earns a celebration the whole family can hear.

SUPPORTING RESOURCE

Open the counting cards.

All twenty cards live in the flashcard library — each with its own page, the original artwork, a download button, print size and short notes for grown-ups on counting it for real at home. When your child owns 1 to 20, the first counting set and the fruit cards make fine revisiting: Numbers 1–10 and Fruits & Vegetables.
